before.problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+2y=8 \\  & x+y=-2 \\  & x+\frac{1}{2}y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- The system has no solution
- The system is consistent independent
- The system is consistent dependent
before.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the following system of equations {3x+2y=8x+y=−2x+12y=5. Which of the following statements are true?

  1. The system has no solution
  2. The system is consistent independent
  3. The system is consistent dependent
a
I and III only
b
III only
c
I only
d
II and III only
e
II only
Submit

decision.explanation: Subtracting twice the second equation from the first gives x=12. Then y=-14. These values also satisfy the third equation: 12+(-14)/2=5. Thus the system has exactly one solution and is consistent independent, so only II is true.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+2y=8 \\  & x+y=-2 \\  & x+\frac{1}{2}y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- The system has no solution
- The system is consistent independent
- The system is consistent dependent
after.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first try to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2 & 8 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 14 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 14 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 14 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y=-2 \\ -y=14.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $y=-14.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-14)=-2\,⟹\,x=12.
$$

 
So,  we conclude that the system is consistent independent.   

As a result, only statement II is true.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+6y=4 \\  & x+(k+1)y=2\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 4 \\ 1 & k+1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 4 \\ 1 & k+1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 4 \\ 0 & k-2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+6y=4 \\  & (k-2)y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=2,$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y.$ So, we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $2x+6y=4.$  

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=2.$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 & -4 \\ 5 & k-6 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & k+9 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned} & -2x+6y=-4 \\  & (k+9)y=0.\end{aligned}

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=-9.$
